newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian shilling firms vs dollar for second week.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian shilling firms vs dollar for second week.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling saw marginal losses in value on the day against the dollar, but appreciated on a weekly basis for the second week in a row, dealers and the central Bank of Tanzania (BoT) said on Friday.
The shilling was posted at a commercial mean rate of 593.9703 to the dollar compared to 593.8218 on Thursday, but up from last Friday's rate of 594.9900.
"It seems to be strengthening for the moment but from an economic point of view I can't see any particular reason for the appreciation," one trader told Reuters.

But he said it could very well had been a result of the formal approval earlier this month by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to grant a $234 million loan to Tanzania in balance of payments support to the central bank.

Prior to the IMF approval on November 8 the shilling went through several weeks of depreciation and traded on November 1 at a commercial mean rate of 597.9600. It started appreciating in the week following the IMF announcement of the new funds to Tanzania, the first since 1992.

"The approval of the IMF loan means that more dollars will flow into the system and will top the current amount," another trader said, adding that export earnings from the agricultural sector also had had an impact this week.

"The shilling has appreciated in part because there has been inflows of dollars as the exports of agricultural products start to flow into the market, but that amount of dollars doesn't really reflect the demand at the moment in the market," he said.

The shilling weakened further against the pound, trading at 1,001.5251, down from 992.4463 last Friday, but traders said as the pound is not widely used in the Tanzanian economy it was of less importance.
